findings.finding: Entry matching uses `what.startswith(w)` with several `EXERCISED` rows carrying `what == ""` (e.g. `"A. Print Intro Banner"`, `"Step 6: Commit and Tag"`). An empty prefix matches any inventory entry in the same (file, section). If a section ever gains a second mechanic/ask/judgement entry, the check fails with "expected exactly 1" — loud, but the error will point at the wrong row (the empty-prefix one), and conversely a genuinely uncovered new entry can be silently "covered" by an empty-prefix row if the other sibling rows were `not_exercised` and happened to be removed. The ambiguity is resolved by failure today only because of the exactly-1 rule.
findings.suggestion: Require non-empty, distinctive prefixes (or exact `what` equality) for rows whose section can hold multiple parts.

findings.finding: Fenced-block coverage accepts any intersecting `NOT_REPLAYED` range (`a <= end and start <= b`). A fenced block that only partially overlaps a `NOT_REPLAYED` range recorded for a different purpose is counted as covered; a future prose reflow that moves a block to straddle an unrelated range would keep P8b green while the block is in fact un-replayed.
findings.suggestion: Require the block to be fully contained in a `NOT_REPLAYED` range (`a <= start and end <= b`), or at minimum log which range covered which block.

findings.finding: The second seeded regression removes the pathspec via a regex over `COMMIT_AND_TAG`'s literal text. This is correctly guarded by `test_the_seed_helpers_change_the_chain_they_claim_to_change`, but the guard only proves the regex matched something; if `COMMIT_AND_TAG` later grows a second ` -- \` segment (e.g. in the verify step), the regex's non-greedy match could strip the wrong segment and the seed would silently become a no-op-different seed while still raising some AssertionError (any `AssertionError` in `check_release_commit_paths` order). The `match="swept in unrelated paths"` mitigates this.
findings.suggestion: Anchor the regex to the `git add`/`git commit` command it targets, or split the chain into named segments.

findings.finding: ASSERTED` is module-global state cleared only in `trace_text`. Any code path that runs a scenario's `check` outside `trace_text` (e.g. a future debugging helper or pytest fixture re-entry after a soft failure) inherits stale assertions, and nested `trace_text` calls from within a `check` would wipe the outer scenario's recorded ACs. Not reachable with today's callers, but fragile.
findings.suggestion: Pass the asserted-set through `Run`/`Scenario` (or a context object) instead of module-global mutable state.

findings.finding: The `FileNotFoundError` shim fabricates `stdout=""`/`stderr` as `str`, while `scratch.run` results elsewhere flow through `_json(done.stdout)`. If any future missing-program key feeds `_json`, `_json("")` behavior (likely `{}`) is relied upon implicitly rather than asserted; today only the `gh` keys hit this path and `step_open_pr`/`release-page` handle it, so this is a robustness note only.
